displayName: Cloud Run Job failure — backtest-sweep / data-backfill

conditions.displayName: A Cloud Run Job execution failed

documentation.content:
A Cloud Run **Job** execution failed. Until FC-096 Phase A nothing in this project watched Jobs, so a Job that failed, or quietly stopped being executed, was invisible. (The battery-degraded policy also matches `cloud_run_job`, but on the battery's own event, not on execution failure.)

Why that matters more for Jobs than for services: **Cloud Scheduler's `jobs:run` is asynchronous.** It records success when the API call returns, not when the execution finishes. A scheduler firing at a Job that fails every time, or at a Job that no longer exists, looks perfectly healthy in the scheduler's own history. This policy is one of two controls that see through that; the other is `/regression`'s `lake_freshness` check, which catches the case where the scheduler is paused or deleted and so never fires at all.

The two Jobs it watches:

- **`backtest-sweep`** — dashboard-submitted scenario sweeps. A failure is usually visible to the submitter as a `failed` row in `scenario_sweeps`; the exception is a container killed before it could write one, which is exactly what this catches.
- **`data-backfill`** — the weekly chain/bars backfill (`backfill-weekly`, Saturdays 08:00 ET). Its failure is the quiet one: nothing downstream breaks immediately, the lake just stops getting fresher, and the first symptom would be a sweep silently materialising cold months later.

**What it actually matches (measured in production).** The Jobs' own logs carry NO LogEntry severity: `src/utils/logger.py` emits a `level` field, not `severity`, so structlog ERROR events (`backfill_symbol_failed`, `sweep_materialise_failed`, ...) never satisfy `severity>=ERROR`. The only entries this filter has ever matched are the platform's `cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fsystem_event` records, "Execution ... has failed to complete" — two so far, both a **non-zero exit**. A task timeout or an OOM kill should produce the same record (platform behaviour, not yet observed here). It does **NOT** see a Job that logs an error and exits 0. FC-098 tracks mapping `level` to `severity`. One condition, deliberately: a log-based policy takes exactly one `conditionMatchedLog`.

Triage:

```
gcloud run jobs executions list --job=data-backfill --region=us-central1 --limit=5
gcloud run jobs executions describe <EXECUTION> --region=us-central1
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_job" AND labels."run.googleapis.com/execution_name"="<EXECUTION>"' --limit=100
```

For `data-backfill` specifically, the per-symbol `backfill_symbol_complete` log lines are the record of what a half-finished run actually wrote — a killed execution leaves no terminal summary — and the Job is idempotent, so the remedy is almost always "execute it again with the same window".

Note the exit-code contract: `--command backfill` exits non-zero when any symbol hit a genuine **failure** (a vendor error, an exception mid-build, a symbol whose bars never arrived, an unusable close) or when a configured chain lake did not take everything it was given. A day skipped for an unmodelled **corporate action** is deliberately NOT one of those: it is counted and logged (`backfill_day_skipped` with `reason=corporate_action`, and `days_skipped_corporate_action` in the summary) but never reaches the exit code. A stock split recurs across the universe and the trailing window slides, so paging every Saturday for the month it takes to age out — on a condition nobody can act on — is how this policy would get muted, and a muted policy is not watching the failures that matter either. If you want to know which days the lake is missing, read the skip events; do not expect an alert for them.
